facts.statement: Brachyuranochampsa was an extinct genus of crocodilian.
facts.quote: Brachyuranochampsa is an extinct genus of crocodilian.

facts.statement: The only robust fossil record of Brachyuranochampsa is the species B. eversolei found in the Middle Eocene of Wyoming.
facts.quote: The only robust occurrence of Brachyuranochampsa is B. eversolei from the Middle Eocene of Wyoming.

facts.statement: The species B. zangerli, found in the lower Bridger Formation at Grizzly Buttes, has been synonymized with the primitive crocodilian "Crocodylus" affinis.
facts.quote: Otra especie, B. zangerli de la formación Bridger inferior en Grizzly Buttes, ha sido sinonimizada con otro crocodiloide primitivo, "Crocodylus" affinis, también conocido de la formación Bridger.

facts.statement: Brachyuranochampsa is an extinct crocodilian genus closely related to the family Crocodylidae but not part of it.
facts.quote: Brachyuranochampsa es un género extinto de crocodiliano cercanamente relacionado con la familia Crocodylidae, pero no formaba parte de la misma.

facts.statement: Brachyuranochampsa lived from the Campanian to the Bartonian stages, between 83.6 and 39.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Bartonian (83.6 to 39.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Brachyuranochampsa is Crocodyloidea.

rejected.statement: The genus Brachyuranochampsa was described by Zangerl in 1944.

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic studies place Brachyuranochampsa as more basal than the crown group Crocodylidae, which includes all living crocodiles.
rejected.quote: Phylogenetic studies have consistently recovered Brachyuranochampsa as more basal than the crown group Crocodylidae, which consists of all extant (living) crocodiles.
